games.title: Key Explorer
games.skillName: Using keys to group and name living things
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise that living things can be grouped in a variety of ways, and explore and use classification keys to help group, identify and name a variety of living things
games.instruction: Follow the clues and tap the group this living thing belongs to.
games.hint: Not quite. Check each clue like a key: look for a backbone, then count the legs and try again.

questions.ask: A ladybird: no backbone, 6 legs, 3 body parts
A garden spider: no backbone, 8 legs, 2 body parts
A snail: no backbone, no legs, soft body and a shell
An earthworm: no backbone, no legs, long body made of segments
A robin: has a backbone, feathers and lays eggs
A fox: has a backbone, fur and feeds its babies milk
A newt: has a backbone, smooth damp skin and lays eggs in water
A daisy: makes its own food and grows flowers

games.title: Power Puzzle
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify common appliances that run on electricity, and recognise some common conductors and insulators, and associate metals with being good conductors
games.instruction: Tap the one that does not belong with the others.
games.hint: Not quite. Ask yourself if it needs electricity, or if electricity can flow through it, then try again.

questions.ask: Which one does NOT run on electricity?
Which one does NOT need electricity to work?
Which material is NOT a good conductor of electricity?
Which material is NOT an electrical insulator?
Which object would NOT let electricity flow through it?
Which object WOULD let electricity flow through it?
Which one is NOT a part you would use to build a simple circuit?
Three of these are metals that conduct electricity. Which is the odd one out?

games.title: Sound Check
games.skillName: Knowing how sounds are made and travel
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify how sounds are made, associating some of them with something vibrating, and recognise that vibrations from sounds travel through a medium to the ear
games.instruction: Is it true or false? Tap your answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about vibrations and how they travel to your ear, then try again.

questions.ask: All sounds are made by something vibrating.
Sound can travel through solids, liquids and gases.
Plucking a guitar string gently makes a louder sound than plucking it hard.
A shorter guitar string makes a lower pitch than a longer one.
Hitting a drum harder makes bigger vibrations.
Sound can travel through empty space where there is no air or anything else.
A sound gets fainter as you move further away from it.
Pitch means how loud or quiet a sound is.

games.title: Circuit Builder
games.skillName: Naming the parts of a simple series circuit
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to construct a simple series electrical circuit, identifying and naming its basic parts, including cells, wires, bulbs, switches and buzzers
games.instruction: Tap the word that fills the gap.
games.hint: Not quite. Picture the circuit as a loop and think about what each part does, then try again.

questions.ask: A bulb will only light if the circuit is a complete ___.
When a switch is open, there is a ___ in the circuit.
When the switch in a complete circuit is closed, the bulb turns ___.
A ___ pushes electricity around a circuit.
The ___ join all the parts of a circuit together.
A ___ makes a sound when the circuit is complete.
A ___ is used to open or close a circuit.
Electricity flows well through metals, so they are good ___.

games.title: Water Cycle Trail
games.skillName: Ordering changes of state in the water cycle
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify the part played by evaporation and condensation in the water cycle, and observe that some materials change state when they are heated or cooled
games.instruction: Tap the step that comes next.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about whether the water is warming up or cooling down, then try again.

questions.ask: Sea water warms in the sun → Water evaporates → Water vapour rises → ?
Water evaporates → Water vapour rises → Vapour cools and condenses → ?
Vapour condenses → Clouds form → Water droplets get heavy → ?
Rain falls → Water flows into rivers → Rivers flow to the sea → ?
Ice → Heat it → Liquid water → Heat it more → ?
Steam from a kettle rises → It hits a cold window → ?
Liquid water → Put it in a freezer → ?
Solid chocolate bar → Hold it in a warm hand → ?

games.title: Tooth and Tummy
games.skillName: Naming teeth and parts of the digestive system
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to describe the simple functions of the basic parts of the digestive system in humans, and identify the different types of teeth in humans and their simple functions
games.instruction: Read the clues and tap what I am.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about the job each part does to your food, then try again.

questions.ask: I am a sharp-edged tooth at the front of your mouth. I cut and bite food. What am I?
I am a pointed, sharp tooth. I tear and rip food such as meat. What am I?
I am a big, wide tooth at the back of your mouth. I grind and crush food. What am I?
I am a tube that carries food from your mouth down to your stomach. What am I?
I am a stretchy bag. I churn your food and mix it with acid. What am I?
I am a long, coiled tube. Goodness from food passes through my walls into the blood. What am I?
I take water out of the waste that is left over after digestion. What am I?
Digestion starts here. Teeth chew and saliva makes food soft and wet. What am I?

games.title: Habitat Watch
games.skillName: Predicting how changing environments affect life
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise that environments can change and that this can sometimes pose dangers to living things
games.instruction: Tap what you think will happen.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what the living things need for food, shelter and safety, then try again.

questions.ask: What will happen to woodland birds if all the trees are cut down?
What will happen to the fish if oil spills into their river?
What will happen to frogs if their pond dries up?
What will happen if people plant a wildflower meadow?
What happens to animals if a busy new road cuts through their wood?
What will happen if a hedgehog eats slugs killed with poison?
What happens to animals when litter is dropped in their habitat?
What will happen to polar bears if the Arctic sea ice melts?

games.title: Food Chain Words
games.skillName: Using food chain words: producer, predator, prey
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to construct and interpret a variety of food chains, identifying producers, predators and prey
games.instruction: Listen to the meaning and tap the matching word.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about who makes food, who eats and who gets eaten, then try again.

questions.ask: A living thing that makes its own food, such as a green plant
An animal that hunts and eats other animals
An animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal
A diagram with arrows that shows what eats what
An animal that eats only plants
An animal that eats only other animals
An animal that eats both plants and other animals
A living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things

games.title: Melt and Boil
games.skillName: Comparing temperatures and rates of evaporation
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to observe that some materials change state when they are heated or cooled, and measure the temperature at which this happens in degrees Celsius (°C); and associate the rate of evaporation with temperature
games.instruction: Tap the one that best answers the question.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about how hot or cold each one is, and how heat changes things, then try again.

questions.ask: Which puddle will dry up the fastest?
Which wet washing will dry the quickest?
Which of these melts at the lowest temperature?
Which of these needs the highest temperature to melt?
Which of these is the hottest?
Which of these places is the coldest?
Which state of matter keeps its own shape the best?
Which state of matter spreads out the most to fill its container?

games.title: Evaporation Lab
games.skillName: Planning fair tests and measuring accurately
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to set up simple practical enquiries and fair tests, and take accurate measurements using standard units and a range of equipment, including thermometers and data loggers
games.instruction: Tap the best way to carry out the investigation.
games.hint: Not quite. Think like a scientist about fair tests and the right equipment, then try again.

questions.ask: Which would you use to measure the temperature of warm water?
Which would you use to measure how much water is left in a dish?
You test if warmth makes water evaporate faster. What should you change?
You test if warmth makes water evaporate faster. What must stay the same?
What is the best way to record the water level in a dish every day for a week?
Dish A in the sun dried in 2 days. Dish B in the shade took 5. What can you conclude?
Which would you use to measure how loud a sound is?
You test which material best muffles a sound. What must stay the same?
